description: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test: statistic sum (o - e)^2 / e over k categories and its p-value, the chi-squared survival function with k - 1 - ddof degrees of freedom

tolerance.reason: For both outputs, as for ttest_1samp. The counts are exact and the statistic is a sum of k positive terms, off by up to about (kappa_s + k) 2^-53 in a careful method, kappa_s being its relative condition number in the expected frequencies (chisquare_rounding_bound); the p-value adds kappa_p = |x f(x) / Q|, about half the statistic in the tail (431 at most where the p-value is a normal double). The largest bound max(kappa_p, 1) (kappa_s + k) 2^-53 there is 4.2e-12 (k = 30 equal expected frequencies, total 1e6, delta 0.1, ddof 1: statistic 888, p 6.1e-169); 5e-12 as for ttest_1samp (tested). P-values that round to 0 (4 points) are exact in any method. SciPy's worst error is 1.9e-13

grid: k in {2, 3, 5, 10, 30} categories; expected frequencies equal or proportional to 1, 2, ..., k; totals 100, 1e4, 1e6; observed counts round(e_i (1 + delta z_i)) with z_i = ((7919 i) mod 1000 - 500) / 1000 and delta in {0.001, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1} (skipped where every count equals its expectation), the expected frequencies rescaled to the counts' sum; ddof 0 and, where k > 2, 1. Statistic from 1e-3 to 2120, p-value from 0 to 1
